name: Dry-Treated Dynamic Climbing Rope (60m, 9.2mm)
hint: Crucial for glacier crevasses, fixed lines, and steep ridge protection.
educationalNote: Dry-treatment prevents ice saturation at sub-zero temperatures, retaining tensile elasticity.

name: Alpine Bod Mountaineering Harness
hint: Ultralight, opens with gloves on, accommodates crampons without stepping through.
educationalNote: Minimalist alpine harnesses feature ice-clipper slots and quick-release leg loops for high-camp ease.

name: Technical Ice Axe / Hybrid Piolet (55cm)
hint: Essential for self-arrest on 50° hard-pack ice and cutting emergency steps.
educationalNote: The pick must bite securely into blue ice; reverse curve geometry aids steep couloir ascents.

name: 12-Point Steel Automatic Crampons
hint: Provides biting traction on blue glacier ice, sérac walls, and wind-scoured ridges.
educationalNote: Steel front points bite reliably into hard water ice; include anti-balling plates to prevent snow accumulation.

name: UIAA-Certified High-Impact Climbing Helmet
hint: Protects against falling rock shards and ice chunks released by warming sun or climbing teams above.
educationalNote: Rockfall in couloirs accelerates at lethal velocity; a certified helmet is non-negotiable from the bergschrund onward.

name: 8,000m Goose Down Expedition Parka / Suit (-40°C)
hint: Shields against deadly wind-chill on the summit push where jet stream winds plunge temperatures past -45°C.
educationalNote: 800+ fill power down with a Gore-Tex Windstopper shell prevents hypothermia during forced bivouacs.

name: Cold-Resistant LED Headlamp (450 Lumens + Spare Lithium Cells)
hint: Required for midnight summit departures (alpine starts) to beat afternoon warming and avalanche cycles.
educationalNote: Standard alkaline batteries freeze dead at -15°C; always pack lithium cells inside internal jacket pockets.

name: High-Altitude Trauma & Diamox Medical Kit
hint: Contains Dexamethasone, Acetazolamide (Diamox), pressure bandages, SAM splint, and blister hydrocolloids.
educationalNote: Prompt administration of Dexamethasone buys critical hours for descent during acute High Altitude Cerebral Edema (HACE).

name: Glacier Sunglasses (Category 4 Protection) + Whiteout Goggles
hint: Snow reflects up to 85% of blinding solar ultraviolet rays, causing debilitating photokeratitis (snow blindness).
educationalNote: Leather side-shields block peripheral glare; Category 4 lenses transmit only 3-8% visible light.

name: 3-Antenna Digital Avalanche Transceiver & Carbon Probe
hint: Emits 457 kHz radio pulses to pinpoint buried companions within the critical 15-minute survival window.
educationalNote: Always switch to transmit mode at Base Camp; never pack beacon next to metallic phones or magnets.

name: Beach Flip Flops
hint: Completely useless on glacial moraines, frostbite hazard at sub-zero temperatures.
educationalNote: Uninsulated rubber provides zero thermal barrier; frostbite will occur within minutes of snow contact.

name: Hardcover Encyclopedia Set (3 Volumes)
hint: Heavy dead weight that exhausts your leg muscles and oxygen supply for zero survival utility.
educationalNote: At 7,000m, every extra kilogram feels like 10kg. Alpinists cut toothbrushes in half to save mere grams.

name: Heavy 100% Cotton Lifestyle Hoodie
hint: Cotton holds moisture like a sponge ('Cotton Kills'). It freezes rigid in high wind, causing rapid hypothermia.
educationalNote: Use only Merino wool or technical synthetic grid fleece that wicks sweat away from the skin.

name: Decorative Rain Umbrella
hint: High-altitude 70 km/h summit squalls will invert and rip an umbrella apart in 3 seconds.
educationalNote: Expedition hardshell jackets with helmet-compatible wire-brim hoods provide true waterproof wind protection.
